violations.requirement: ptr.offset requires the result to stay within the same allocated object (in bounds). msync needs a valid mapped range.
violations.explanation: This is a safe public function. It forwards the caller's offset and len to MmapInner::flush without checking them. The doc comment says they must be in bounds, but nothing enforces that. An out-of-range offset makes self.ptr.offset(offset) leave the mapping, which is UB. It can also pass an invalid range to msync.

violations.requirement: ptr.offset requires the result to stay within the same allocated object (in bounds). msync needs a valid mapped range.
violations.explanation: This is a safe public function. It forwards an unchecked offset and len to MmapInner::flush_async. An offset or len beyond the mapping makes self.ptr.offset(aligned_offset) go out of bounds, which is UB.

violations.requirement: The offset must stay within the bounds of the mapped allocation. The range passed to msync must be valid.
violations.explanation: This is a safe pub function. It does not check offset or len against self.len. It also computes the alignment from (ptr + offset) but then subtracts that from offset. self.ptr.offset(offset) can therefore fall outside the mapping when the caller passes bad values.

violations.requirement: The offset must stay within the bounds of the mapped allocation. The range passed to msync must be valid.
violations.explanation: This is a safe pub function. It does not validate offset or len against self.len before calling self.ptr.offset(aligned_offset) and msync.
